questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Since I started planning my exchange during the pandemic and did not know when all the restrictions would end I wanted to optimize my chances of the exchange actually taking place, which is the reason why I chose a destination in Europe and one of KU's partner universities. I also wanted to go somewhere where I would at the very least have a passing knowledge of the language so I would have a chance of understanding what has going on around me when I was not the one directly spoken to. Lastly I liked that at TiHo you could choose to which clinics you were going to spend your time in, so that you could focus on your area of interest.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy in terms of enrollment, but fairly difficult in terms of schedule/ program for my stay.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a meeting with my contact person who helped me get enrolled and handed me som papers with a map of the campuses, information on how to access the e-mail etc. Then I was given a tour of the clinic by the veterinarian in charge of international students there and shown to the service where I was to spend my first week. I did not get the full introduction until the end of the week when the next of the clinical cycles were starting up. This was when the new students and I was presented with the schedule, got another tour of the clinic and got an introduction to the different services we would be cycling through and how the cycle worked.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I would have really liked to have received a schedule or program before arriving so that I knew what to expect going in.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. My contact person had encouraged me to find housing on my own and supplied me with links to different dorms and to a webpage with shared flats (WGs). I started applying for dorms approximately 3 months before departure, but non had any rooms available for the time I needed it. I started to apply for WGs about a month before departure, which gave me a better response. I liked living in a WG, so if you want to live off campus I would recommend doing that since it is a great way to get to know new people. TiHo also offers housing and a room was reserved for me, so there was no stress that I would arrive without somewhere to stay.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The areas around the small animal clinic (Bult, Kleefeld, Südstadt) are rather suburban, so if you want to live somewhere more urban go for the north of the city (Nordstadt, Calenberger-Neustadt), which is where the main university of the city is located. I lived in Calenberger-neustadt close to Königsworther Platz which is around 6 km from the small animal clinic and it took me around 25 min. on bike or by public transportation to get there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you apply for a WG expect to go through an interview/ casting so that you and your potential flat mates can get a feel for each other.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After receiving a spot through the KU application I was put in contact with my contact person who sent me an application form I need to fill out to be provisionally accepted. Later I was asked what clinics I was interested in staying at during my exchange. I was officially enrolled after arriving at TiHo.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had a contact person at the international office who I could ask questions and who would remind me of deadline etc. which was great.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I expressed interest in spending time at the small animal clinic and the exotics clinic and was awarded a spot in the clinical cycle in the small animal clinic.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing, it was really easy and I felt like I was well guided through the process.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The amount that the different vets liked to teach was rather varied which lead to how much you got out of the different weeks/services being somewhat varied as well. The communication was also not always all that great making it somewhat unclear what was expected from us and at times made everything a bit chaotic since we were unsure of where we needed to be at a given time etc.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I felt like I was well equipped to take on the course and that the level of the course was good.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Since TiHo is a referral hospital they do not really do the first consultations/ general practitioner stuff such as vaccinations, chipping etc. Since the consultations were generally more specialized the students did not really have any patient responsibility, which lead it to be somewhat limited how much we got to do during a consultation (generally we got to take an anamnesis here and there and do a general examination, but it was a lot of standing around and listening). Whenever blood samples were taken one of the students would generally get to do it, and the same was the case with placing venous catheters. Since we did not have patient responsibility we also did not have to write the medical records or going home letters etc. Since we did not have to do any paperwork we unfortunately sometimes ended up with days with quite a lot of time of us just sitting around waiting for something to happen/ a patient to show up, especially when there was not all that many patients booked in. 

They also have quite a few interns and phd students who I sometimes felt was prioritized over the PJ students*, since they where usually the ones who got to be 1st assistant in surgeries, did the anamnesis, had to write the medical records and so on. 

At TiHo they hospitalize way more patients than at KU which also meant that we had to spend far more time looking after these patients (around 3 out of 10 weeks spread out over day-, night-, and weekend shifts) which I did not feel like I I gained all that much from since I rarely knew the patients and why they were receiving the treatment that they received and usually did not have the time to go look them up to gain insight into their medical history.

*PJ students = Practical year students

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I did a practical year cycle at the small animal clinic

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Since I only took one course I will just list the services I liked the best. I really liked neurology, dermatology, ophthalmology and ultrasound as well as reproduction despite there unfortunately being too many people and too few cases for the week I was there.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: An administrational fee of €352

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and rent was generally more inexpensive than back home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not take advantage of the opportunities as much as I would have liked since we had very long days (8-17 or sometimes longer eg if you were in surgery) and had weekend- and nightshifts.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Hochschule Sport which offers different sports for free/ low fees to enrolled students

ESN (Erasmus student network) - I was not made aware of this organization by TiHo, but by one of my flatmates who had done an exchange herself. They arrange trips and events for international students and whatever germans who want to join in as well in the city and surrounding area.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you are there during the spring/summer I would recommend going canoeing/kayaking/SUPing on the Leine/Ihme rivers, since it gets pretty hot in the city and is a nice way to spend a hot day. The city is pretty flat and has a lot of bike lanes so if you have a pair of rollerblades I would recommend bringing them since it seems like a fun way to explore the city. The zoo and Herrenhäuser Garten are also worth a visit.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: When you get enrolled and pay the administrational fee you also get a semester ticket which allows you to travel on public transportation throughout all of Lower Saxony for free. You can therefore go to cities such as Bremen or Hamburg for a day trip at no extra cost, which is a fun way to spend a day.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy since the cultures are rather similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Speak German since a lot of the students are very insecure about their English or speak it poorly. I did not really follow this advise myself if I am being honest, but it worked out and my understanding was generally good enough that I understood it when they spoke German to me and could help supply English words if they spoke English to me and were struggling finding the right words.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They are way less digitalized than we are in Denmark and pretty much everything gets printed out and there are way less computers just standing around where you can look up the patients. The germans were also generally rather bad at taking breaks to make sure that they get to eat lunch. You could also feel that there was somewhat more of a hierarchy compared to what I am used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How much they care for animals. I was continually surprised how far a lot of owners were willing to go in terms of treatment of their animals and how dog friendly of a place Germany is.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Brush up on your German, it will make life way easier for you
2) Do not bring any clothes for the clinic, you get some at the clinic. The only thing you need to bring is a stethoscope and maybe a belt since it can be a challenge to find pants that fit
3) Bring/ rent a bike, it is a great way to get around the city - especially to get home when you have nightshifts

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
During a cycle you rotate through the different services or a combination of services spending a week in each service or pair of services eg derma and ultrasound or ophthalmology and oncology. You rotate in pairs or a 3 person group as was the case for me since the cycle was already filled so I was a bit of an extra. On Mondays we would have a 2 hour seminar in the afternoon and on Thursday we would have a 1 hour x-ray case based seminar, so on these days we got to leave the clinic early otherwise days were generally from 8 till 17. The cycle include one week of nightshifts, one weekend of dayshifts, and one weekend of nightshifts.

If you have a dog and you want to bring it you can. The students have a room where we ate lunch etc. and you can keep your dog there in a crate while you are at the clinic, which quite a few of the students did.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Gaining a really good understanding of the language, so that by the end of my stay I could more or less understand everything being said to me even if I could not respond as well in German.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language since it did lead me to sometimes not participating as much as I probably could because I was not always sure I understood a question correctly.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: My German proficiency was me taking German back in folkeskolen and gymnasiet and then not really using it since, so if that is the same for you do not let that scare you off of going to Germany on exchange. The people there were generally really nice about letting me answer in English or switching to English around me if I was the only one there.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
